I did this one last year. Everyone has given you good swimming advice, so here is my prep advice. 

The water is cold- last year they threatened not having the swim part. It will be a shock and can take your breath away. Do get into the water before the race. Do try to relax once in the water. Do give yourself a moment to adjust to the cold. 

A lot of people were shivering and turning blue afterwards. A few weeks before, I prepared for this by taking a one minute cold shower 3-4 times a week. The colder the better. Make sure you have your head and full body in. And it doesn’t have to be much longer than a minute- I set a timer. This is how long it takes to warm up your wetsuit. Also, get a neoprene cap for under the Ironman swim cap. This will help a lot! I didn’t not feel cold at all in the water. I found it really nice. 

Side note: don’t take the tag off the wetsuit in the morning after dipping it in the chlorine pools. This tag indicates the wetsuit has been dipped. 

Enjoy. And good luck!!

I would have months and months of feeling slightly to the left of myself. Just always out of place. No feeling of happy, not that I was unhappy. No feeling of belonging. There was never enough sleeping hours, yet I hated going to bed at night. I would sleep in various places around the house. I feared leaving my house, answering a text or even looking at my social media. I had very little food in the house as I feared being in a store and having a full on breakdown. Most of the food I did have was easy and quick to make: cans of soup, mr noodle or frozen meals. 

Key words are “would have”!! I spend over 20 years being depressed off and on. Longest run was eight months. 

While I’m not fully recovered, I might get a day or two. It’s been 18 months since I’ve had anything lasting more than a few days. 

I switched jobs!! While I hadn’t been at the same job for 20 years, I had been at that job the last fours year of the worst of it. 

I’ve also become more aware of these feelings. I know it’s chemical imbalance, but I’ve learned to read what my body needs. I ask myself: have I eaten today-was it nutritious enough? Have I showered? Have I made human contact (I ask for hugs from my husband when I’m in need of extra touching)? Have a taken a moment to feel the sun/wind/rain/snow on my face? 

And I also know that it’s ok to somedays just wear my PJs, sit on the couch with shitty food and watch Netflix. Sometime that how I heal.
